Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with acute pain and swelling of the right knee. The reported
mechanism of injury is consistent with the kind and force of the impact observed. Imaging and physical examination findings
clearly confirm the knee injury, and no prior injury to the same body region is known from the patient history. Care was delivered
over 29 visits, wihch is somewhat longer than typically expected for this type of injury, with progression addressed through
reassessment at each stage. Conservative management included physical therapy, activity modification, and anti-inflammatory
medication, with gradual improvement in range of motion and strength. Billing records reviewed for the episode of care show no
repeated charges for the same services. Ongoing follow-up and a home exercise program have been recommended, and the
patient is expected to return to baseline activity with continued rehabilitation.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
